title: Self-barrier CuMn bitline merges conductor and diffusion barrier
idea: Combine the bitline conductor and its TiN/WSix barrier into one Cu-0.5%Mn alloy fill; a post-fill anneal drives Mn to the dielectric interface where it forms a ~2 nm MnSiOx barrier in situ, replacing the W/TiN bitline stack (later capacitor anneals capped below ~500 C).
why: Removes bitline tungsten (China ~80%) and the barrier deposition; ~2x lower bitline resistance allows longer bitlines and fewer sense-amp stripes (~5-8% die area, periphery wall).

title: Hydrogen backside cooling shares the fab forming-gas recycle loop
idea: Combine the chuck's backside-cooling gas with the fab's existing H2 supply: run 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity ~0.18 W/m-K vs He ~0.15) under wafers in etch/CVD, recapture it through a palladium-membrane purifier and return it to the forming-gas anneal header.
why: Eliminates the largest in-fab helium use while Qatar's ~30% is offline; equal or better heat transfer; H2 can be electrolyzed on site in the U.S.

title: Silicon-skull cold crucible pulls Czochralski ingots without quartz
idea: Combine induction skull melting with Czochralski pulling: a segmented water-cooled copper crucible plus RF induction holds a frozen silicon skull so the melt only touches silicon; oxygen for internal gettering is supplied by controlled O2/N2 gas doping instead of crucible dissolution.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% concentration) and its consumable cost from DRAM wafer supply; tunable oxygen improves wafer uniformity (trade: +20-40% melt energy).

title: HBM die thinning by layer splitting so parent wafers recycle
idea: Combine HBM's mandatory 30-50 um die thinning with porous-silicon layer transfer: build core dies on epi above a buried porous-Si cleave plane, split the 40 um device layer off after carrier bonding instead of grinding ~700 um to slurry, then re-polish and re-epi the parent for 10+ reuses.
why: HBM grinds ~95% of each wafer's silicon away; reuse cuts prime wafer, polysilicon and crucible demand per HBM bit ~80-90% and removes grinding water.

title: Molybdenum dioxide electrode replaces ruthenium and templates rutile TiO2
idea: Combine the capacitor bottom electrode with the dielectric's crystal seed: metallic, rutile-type ALD MoO2 plays the templating role RuO2 plays in lab stacks, nucleating rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) at <=400 C, with an Al-doped TiO2 interface layer to cut leakage.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (needs k ~70) without ruthenium (South Africa ~85-90%); Mo is U.S.-mined; ~1.5-2x Cs at the same aspect ratio.

title: Abatement waste heat drives membrane distillation back to ultrapure water
idea: Combine the fab's 50-80 C waste heat (thermal abatement, compressors, heat-pumped chiller return) with membrane distillation: rinse and scrubber effluent passes against a PFAS-free polypropylene/ceramic hydrophobic membrane so only vapor crosses, yielding near-UPW feed that needs only final ion-exchange polishing.
why: Recovers 60-80% of rinse water with free heat, cutting fresh intake 2-3x and RO pumping energy; makes arid U.S. sites viable.

title: Tin-oxo dry resist converts itself into the etch hardmask
idea: Combine EUV photoresist and hardmask: vapor-deposited tin-oxo-cluster resist is exposed and dry-developed, then an in-situ O2/H2O plasma densifies the remaining pattern into SnO2 that serves directly as the etch hardmask, deleting fluorinated-PAG resist, spin-on carbon and SiON layers.
why: Drops PFAS-bearing photoacid generators and 2-3 film depositions per critical layer; dry develop cuts solvent waste ~5-10x; lower dose frees scarce EUV scanner time.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching revives the deep silicon trench capacitor
idea: Combine catalytic metal-assisted chemical etching (Ag nanodots sinking through Si in HF/H2O2) with the old trench-DRAM capacitor: block-copolymer-placed dots carve 15 nm holes at >200:1 aspect ratio in silicon, catalyst is stripped in HNO3, then ALD ZrO2/TiN lines the holes.
why: Goes far past the 60-75:1 plasma-etch limit without fluorocarbon gases or plasma etch tools; Cs >10 fF; capital for the hardest etch drops ~10x.

title: HBM base die merged into an active interposer bridge
idea: Combine the HBM logic base die and the silicon interposer: the interposer region under each stack carries the PHY, ECC and TSV landing logic, so core dies hybrid-bond straight onto it and the separate base die and its microbump layer disappear.
why: Saves ~100 mm2 of silicon per stack (~10-15% of package silicon) and one SnAg bump layer, and removes one assembly yield loss from the HBM TSV tax.

title: Barrierless molybdenum contacts silicide themselves during the fill anneal
idea: Combine contact barrier, fill and silicide into one ALD Mo step from a fluorine-free chloride precursor (MoO2Cl2): Mo deposits directly on Si and a ~600 C anneal forms a MoSi2 interface, deleting the Ti/TiN liner and WF6 tungsten fill.
why: Tungsten-free and fluorine-free contacts; 20-40% lower contact resistance because no barrier eats the narrow via; Mo is U.S.-mined.

title: Getter-coated chamber walls replace helium-loop cryopumps
idea: Combine the chamber liner with the vacuum pump: sputter a TiZrV non-evaporable getter film on PVD chamber liners that pumps H2, CO and H2O at room temperature and reactivates during normal bake/seasoning, with small turbo pumps handling argon.
why: Retires helium-compressor cryopump loops and their makeup helium and ~7 kW compressors per tool; fewer regeneration downtimes.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-silicon oxide gain cell with graded self-insulator
idea: Combine channel and gate insulator in one co-sputtered Zn-Sn-Si-O film whose Si fraction ramps from ~5% (semiconducting channel) to ~50% (amorphous insulator) in a single chamber pass, forming a 2T gain-cell storage transistor with no indium, no gallium and no separate gate-oxide ALD.
why: IGZO gain cells depend on indium (China ~60%) and gallium (China ~98%, export-controlled); ZTSO uses abundant Zn, Sn, Si and one deposition replaces two while keeping wide-bandgap ultra-low leakage.

title: Skip hafnium-zirconium separation: qualify natural-ratio zirconium precursors
idea: Combine the two elements nature already combines: electronics needs no nuclear-grade Hf/Zr separation, so qualify ALD precursors made directly from unseparated zircon (~2% Hf) for ZrO2 capacitors and specify periphery dielectrics as natural (Zr,Hf)O2.
why: Deletes the costly solvent-extraction separation step (a large share of precursor cost) and makes hafnium non-critical for DRAM.

title: All-carbon capacitor mold etched with oxygen instead of fluorocarbons
idea: Combine mold material and strip chemistry: replace the oxide/nitride capacitor mold with amorphous carbon, etch holes in O2/N2/COS plasma with sulfur sidewall passivation, deposit electrodes, then remove the mold in the same O2 ash rather than an HF wet strip.
why: Removes C4F6/C4F8/CHF3 (high-GWP, PFAS-adjacent) from DRAM's hardest etch and the HF strip; dry removal ends pillar collapse; carbon etches 2-3x faster, so fewer etch tools.

title: Polysilicon plant SiCl4 waste becomes synthetic silica crucible liners
idea: Combine the Siemens polysilicon byproduct stream with crucible making: flame-hydrolyze waste SiCl4 into ultra-pure synthetic silica soot, fuse it as the melt-contacting 3-5 mm inner layer, and build the outer bubble-composite body from ordinary quartz sand.
why: Breaks the Spruce Pine >80% high-purity-quartz chokepoint by turning a waste (~10+ kg SiCl4 per kg poly) into the scarce input, sited at U.S. polysilicon plants.

title: Nanoimprint template also prints the self-assembly guide pattern
idea: Combine nanoimprint and directed self-assembly: one imprint stamps sparse 40-80 nm guide posts plus a chemically patterned brush, then a high-chi block copolymer fills in 4-8x denser features and heals imprint defects for capacitor-hole and active arrays.
why: Replaces 2-3 EUV/ArF multi-patterning layers with an imprint tool ~1/10 the cost of an EUV scanner, cutting single-supplier dependence and ~1 MW/tool energy.

title: Replacement buried wordline: sacrificial poly early, aluminum fill late
idea: Combine logic's replacement-metal-gate flow with the buried wordline: a sacrificial poly-Si plug sits in the trench through the hot activation steps, then is removed and the trench filled with Al-Cu by low-temperature CVD, with all later steps (low-temp ALD capacitor) kept <=450 C.
why: Removes the largest tungsten volume in a DRAM die using abundant aluminum; lower narrow-line resistance lets wordlines double in length, cutting sub-wordline drivers in the ~49% periphery.

title: Fixed-abrasive pad releases its own silica, ending ceria STI polish
idea: Combine pad and slurry: a polyurethane pad loaded with sol-gel silica nodules releases fresh colloidal silica as it is conditioned, while an amino-acid additive in plain water supplies the oxide/nitride selectivity ceria normally provides.
why: Removes cerium (China-dominated rare earth) from STI/ILD CMP and cuts slurry volume, water and waste ~70%.

title: ALD exhaust cold-trap reclaims precursors for on-site repurification
idea: Combine the ALD foreline trap with a precursor refinery: a staged cryogenic trap captures the >90% of Zr/Hf/Ti metal-organic precursor that passes unreacted during purge pulses, and an on-site fractional distillation unit repurifies it to 6N for re-feed.
why: Cuts metal precursor consumption 3-5x and abatement energy; the capacitor stack burns the most ALD cycles in the fab.

title: Datacenter DIMM salvage reborn as tested CXL memory pools
idea: Combine server decommissioning with CXL memory expansion: desolder DRAM packages from retired DDR4/DDR5 modules, retest and speed-bin them, and mount them on CXL Type-3 cards whose controller hides mixed timing and maps weak rows out.
why: Every reused retired bit displaces a new wafer start; at 4x prices, recovering even 5% of supply needs zero fab capital, zero helium and zero quartz.

title: Nuclear SMR co-located fab: one reactor powers, chills, purifies
idea: Combine an SMR's electricity, its steam and its low-grade heat into the fab's three biggest utilities: power for tools, steam-driven absorption chillers for process cooling, and waste heat for thermal desalination of UPW feedwater from brackish sources.
why: Cuts utility energy cost and carbon ~30% for a ~300 MW fab and decouples siting from fresh water and grid congestion, raising U.S. manufacturability.

title: Top dummy die etched into a water microchannel cold plate
idea: Combine HBM's topmost dummy spacer die with a cold plate: deep-etch 100 um microchannels into it and pump water/glycol through, replacing two-phase immersion in fluorinated (Novec-type, being phased out) fluids for hot AI racks.
why: Removes PFAS coolants; ~20 C lower HBM junction temperature roughly halves retention leakage, so refresh rate and its 16-33% idle power share halve.

title: Laser-polymer spalling slices ingots into wafers without kerf
idea: Combine subsurface IR laser modification with polymer stress spalling: a focused 1.3-2 um laser writes a damage plane 775 um deep, and a chilled polymer film bonded on top cracks the wafer off along it, replacing multi-wire sawing that turns ~40% of the ingot into kerf.
why: ~40-60% more wafers per ingot, so proportionally fewer quartz crucibles, less polysilicon energy and no saw slurry water.

title: Deuterated nitride supporter doubles as an interface-passivation reservoir
idea: Combine the capacitor's existing SiN support lattice with trap passivation (zero added masks): deposit it from SiD4/ND3 so it stores ~20 at.% deuterium, which diffuses down during later anneals and passivates access-transistor interface/GIDL traps with stronger Si-D bonds.
why: Trims the <=13 fA leakage tail that sets refresh; halving it doubles the refresh interval (~23 fJ/bit saved, 5-10% bandwidth back) and replaces high-pressure H2/D2 anneals.

title: One block mask lets capacitor ZrO2 double as periphery gate
idea: Combine the cell-capacitor ZrO2 ALD with the periphery high-k gate: periphery moves to a gate-last module whose trenches are opened by the single added mask, so the same ZrO2 run coats capacitor and periphery gates, with La/Al dipoles setting Vt.
why: Removes hafnium entirely and one full HKMG dielectric module (~6-8 steps); ALD tool demand per wafer start down ~10%.

title: Landing pad and capacitor bottom electrode become one TiN body
idea: Combine the tungsten landing pad and the bottom electrode (zero added masks, same landing-pad mask): pattern the pads in TiN and grow the electrode cylinder conformally from them, so there is no W/TiN interface and no WF6 fill.
why: Removes one of the largest tungsten volumes per die and a resistive interface; fewer depositions; TiN's higher resistivity is harmless over the pad's short length.

title: Reclaimed monitor wafers reborn under thick device-grade epitaxy
idea: Combine wafer reclaim with epitaxy (zero masks): repolish reclaimed monitor and prime-reject wafers, grow a 3-5 um device-grade epi layer, and add a backside polysilicon gettering layer to replace oxygen-precipitate gettering.
why: Monitor/test wafers are ~10-20% of fab wafer use; turning them into product substrates cuts virgin wafer, crucible and polysilicon demand ~10-15% and epi lowers the defect-driven leakage tail.

title: Titanium-silicide strapped dual-work-function polysilicon wordline
idea: Combine the old poly gate with a self-aligned silicide strap (zero added masks): fill the buried-wordline trench with in-situ doped poly, recess it, then sputter Ti and anneal so TiSi2 forms only on exposed poly, leaving lower n+ poly near the channel and the strap for conduction.
why: Removes buried-wordline tungsten with abundant Ti and Si; work-function engineering of the poly reduces GIDL, lengthening refresh intervals.

title: Antiferroelectric zirconia biased near its field-induced transition boosts charge
idea: Combine paraelectric storage with antiferroelectric switching (zero added masks): tune ALD ZrO2 thickness and Si/Al doping so its tetragonal phase sits just below the field-induced polar transition at the storage voltage, giving an effective k ~50-60 across the operating window.
why: ~1.5x stored charge per capacitor without higher aspect ratio or hafnium, or equal charge at lower VARY (CV2 energy).

title: Gray-tone mask and dual-tone resist merge two EUV layers
idea: Combine two critical layers in one EUV exposure: a gray-tone mask (partial-transmission absorber) gives two dose levels that a dual-tone resist resolves into two solubility states, developed sequentially (positive, then negative) into two stacked hardmasks; this removes a mask rather than adding one.
why: Cuts one of 5-7 EUV layers (~15-20% of per-wafer EUV time freed), easing the single-supplier chokepoint and ~1 MW/tool energy.

title: Capacitor plate electrode doubles as an in-field annealing heater
idea: Combine the common top plate with a Joule heater: the one added mask cuts the plate into serpentine segments with two contacts each, so during idle maintenance the controller pulses a sub-array to ~150-200 C for seconds to anneal out variable-retention (VRT) trap cells.
why: Recovers retention-tail cells in service, extending module life and usable yield ~1.5-2x and reducing demand for scarce new bits.

title: Two-pass Czochralski purifies upgraded metallurgical silicon, then grows prime
idea: Combine purification and crystal growth (zero masks): a fast sacrificial pull from low-B/P upgraded metallurgical silicon dumps metals into the melt tail by segregation (k ~1e-5 to 1e-8 for Fe, Cu, Ni); the clean section is crushed and repulled as a slow prime ingot.
why: Skips most of the Siemens process (~50-100 kWh/kg, chlorosilane chemistry), roughly halving polysilicon energy; B/P must be removed upstream by slag refining.

title: Aluminum-doped zinc oxide top plate replaces germanium SiGe fill
idea: Combine the plate electrode and pillar-forest gap fill (zero added masks, same plate mask): replace the boron-doped poly-SiGe plate fill over the TiN top electrode with ALD/CVD ZnO:Al, which fills conformally at ~200 C and conducts ~1e-3 ohm-cm.
why: Removes germanium (China-dominated, export-controlled) and GeH4 from every DRAM wafer; low temperature protects the dielectric.

title: Puller heater coils also generate the melt-damping magnetic field
idea: Combine the CZ heater and the melt-stabilizing magnet (zero masks): drive segmented heater coils with phase-shifted AC so they produce a traveling magnetic field that damps melt convection, replacing superconducting cusp magnets and their helium cryostats.
why: Helium-free magnetic CZ for 300 mm DRAM wafers; drops ~$1-2M of magnet capital per puller and magnet power.

title: Supercritical CO2 dries capacitor pillars without collapse or water
idea: Combine final rinse/dry with mechanical protection (zero masks): after the mold strip, displace water with a co-solvent and then closed-loop supercritical CO2 (zero surface tension) so tall pillars never see capillary force.
why: Ends pillar collapse that caps aspect ratio, enabling AR ~100 for more charge and fewer SiN supporter layers, while cutting final-rinse UPW and IPA.

title: Polymer-copper hybrid bond whose bonding polymer becomes the underfill
idea: Combine HBM die bonding and underfill: the one added mask patterns a photo-definable BCB/polyimide around Cu pads; at bonding, Cu-Cu interdiffuses while the polymer flows and cures into a void-free underfill, eliminating SnAg microbumps and capillary underfill.
why: Removes tin and silver from HBM stacks, shrinks bond pitch ~40 to ~10 um for more TSVs, and raises stack yield against the 20-30% TSV-tax loss.

title: Self-ordering anodic alumina pores form the capacitor-hole array
idea: Combine anodization's spontaneous hexagonal pore ordering with the capacitor array: deposit ~2 um Al, the one added mask imprints pore-nucleation dimples aligned to landing pads, and voltage-set anodization (~2.5 nm pitch per volt) grows straight alumina pores at >100:1 that serve as the mold.
why: Replaces the hardest multi-patterning layer and the fluorocarbon high-AR etch with a wet electrochemical step using abundant aluminum and oxalic acid; mold height set only by Al thickness, ~2x Cs.

title: Periphery wafer from U.S. legacy fabs bonded onto cell array
idea: Combine image-sensor wafer bonding with DRAM: build sense amps, decoders and I/O on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing U.S. mature fabs and only the array on the DRAM wafer; the array wafer adds exactly one mask (hybrid-bond pads) and drops its periphery masks.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die; moving it to EUV-free, depreciated U.S. fabs cuts DRAM-fab area per bit ~40% and frees the array from periphery thermal budget.

title: Reusable silicon-nitride crucible supplies the wafer's nitrogen doping
idea: Combine crucible and dopant source (zero masks): a dense, non-wetting Si3N4 crucible is reused across 10-50 melts, and its slow dissolution supplies the 1e14-1e15 cm-3 nitrogen DRAM wafers already need for void control, with oxygen added by gas.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine quartz crucible consumable entirely and a separate nitrogen-doping step; risk is nitride precipitate inclusions.

title: Topcoat-free immersion resist via self-segregating siloxane additive
idea: Combine resist and immersion topcoat (zero masks): a hydrocarbon-siloxane block additive floats to the resist surface during spin coat and forms the hydrophobic water barrier normally made by fluorinated topcoats and fluorinated surface additives.
why: Removes PFAS-class topcoats and one coat/bake step from 10+ ArF immersion layers per DRAM wafer ahead of PFAS restrictions.

title: Single stitch-metal mask harvests independent quarter-dies at wafer edge
idea: Combine a tiled die with wafer-edge recovery: the die is built as four self-sufficient quadrants, and the one added top-metal stitch mask ties them into a full die in complete fields while edge partial fields are left as independent quarter-capacity dies.
why: Recovers ~3-6% more bits per wafer from edge silicon now scrapped, equivalently less wafer, crucible and energy per bit.

title: Arsenic-free n-type junctions via phosphorus epi and laser activation
idea: Combine source/drain formation with doping (zero masks): selective in-situ phosphorus-doped Si:P epi grows only on exposed Si, and nanosecond laser melt activates it, replacing arsenic implants and furnace spikes.
why: Removes arsine/arsenic (China-dominated) and toxic-gas handling; lower thermal budget saves energy and limits diffusion that worsens cell GIDL.

title: Flowable oxide fills and self-planarizes, ending ceria STI polish
idea: Combine trench fill and planarization (zero masks): flowable-CVD silazane oxide fills STI and levels like a liquid, then a timed dry etch-back endpointed on the pad nitride replaces the ceria CMP and post-CMP clean.
why: Removes rare-earth ceria slurry and hundreds of liters of UPW per wafer for CMP/cleans; flowable fill also voids less in 10 nm array trenches.

title: DRAM's own capacitor forest replaces package decoupling MLCCs
idea: Combine the cell-capacitor process with power-delivery decoupling: the one added mask shorts blocks of storage capacitors in periphery gaps and die corners into on-die decaps (>1 uF/mm2, since 5 fF per ~900 nm2 cell), deleting most BaTiO3/Ni MLCCs and tantalum capacitors on HBM and DIMM substrates.
why: Sidesteps recurring MLCC and tantalum (DRC) shortages; quieter supply lets VDD margin drop ~5%, a direct CV2 energy cut.

title: Silicon-on-nothing voids isolate cells using only silicon and hydrogen
idea: Combine isolation and body insulation via the empty-space-in-silicon effect: the one added mask etches arrays of deep holes under active-area ends, and a high-temperature H2 anneal lets silicon surface-migrate to seal them into buried voids that cut leakage paths beneath the access transistor.
why: Cuts the junction leakage tail (refresh energy ~30-50% lower) and replaces part of the STI fill oxide and its CMP with nothing but silicon and hydrogen.

title: Subtractive molybdenum bitlines with self-aligned air-gap spacers
idea: Combine bitline patterning with spacer formation (zero added masks, existing bitline mask): blanket Mo is etched subtractively in Cl2/O2, then a non-conformal cap pinches off over the gaps, leaving k=1 air spacers.
why: Tungsten-free bitline from U.S.-mined Mo; ~30% lower bitline capacitance gives more sense signal or longer bitlines (fewer sense amps) and lower CV2 energy per access.
